correctness.rationale: The Hamiltonian gives exactly tr(T_L² T^(N−2)); T_L=cT+dσ_x and Cayley–Hamilton reproduce the three terms in (1). In q,u notation their coefficients are u(1−q²), u^−1−2q+u q² and 2q(1−u q), respectively. At x=0 their even signed combination is u−u^−1; the signed odd derivative is Nu−(N−2)/u−2q, giving the stated unique positive threshold below 1. For L≤0 the endpoint x=1 has positive value and the strictly positive interior nodes cos(jπ/(N−1)) have signs (−1)^j. On the positive side j=0,…,m−1 gives m−1 sign-change intervals for either N=2m or 2m+1. Parity gives their negatives and, when odd, x=0, hence N−2 distinct real zeros before testing the central gap. For N=3 the closest positive node is the endpoint 1: use (3), not the interior-node formula. The positive signed odd derivative yields the two additional central real roots; at either threshold the central multiplicity and the distinct outer roots exhaust the degree, hence the multiplicities are exactly two and three. Below threshold evaluating i^−N F_N(iy) (divided by y for odd N) gives a negative initial value and positive leading behavior, hence a pair ±iy, which exhausts the remaining degree and proves simplicity. For the fugacity map write F_N(x)=x^εR(x²), ε=N mod 2, and x²=(z+1)²/(4(1−q²)z). A nonzero pair gives a quadratic in z with product 1; real |x|<1 gives two simple circle zeros, imaginary x gives negative distinct reciprocal zeros. Each factor x² raises the order at z=−1 by two and x^ε by ε. This removes branch ambiguity. The L≥0 circle property uses the classical ferromagnetic theorem. The result concerns the common L changing sign, not varying one edge independently.
residual_risks: The n=3 endpoint and fugacity multiplicities require the explicit arguments recorded above. The finite verifier does not certify the root-count theorem; no result on unequal couplings is inferred.

Flipping the impurity spin changes both bond signs but also flips the field at that site, so it does not preserve the uniform-field polynomial. Summing that spin produces the endpoint weight 2 cosh(h+L(s_2+s_N)), not merely a constant-coupling replacement seam in a uniform field.

originality.rationale: The exact two-bond impurity partition model and its transfer evaluation are prior art; the nonnegative-coupling circle result is also prior. A distinct single-frustrated-bond result anticipates the qualitative parity and collision pattern very closely, but has another bond geometry and different critical formulas. The surviving result is the sharp two-equal-bond threshold at negative coupling, with exhaustive off-circle count, real location and odd triple collision for this topology.
residual_risks: Unavailable full texts and unexamined general nonferromagnetic results may supply additional coverage; no global priority claim. The prior one-seam theorem considerably reduces novelty attributable to the shared pattern alone.

value.rationale: A single physical impurity atom naturally has two incident bonds. For this geometry the result identifies when a genuinely antiferromagnetic impurity preserves the circle: odd rings tolerate a nonzero negative interval, even rings do not, and failure is confined to one negative real reciprocal pair. The exact thresholds and multiplicity control are useful for finite Ising zero analysis and differ substantively from a one-seam reparameterization; no value is assigned to the covered ferromagnetic portion by itself.
residual_risks: Finite, equal-defect model only. No thermodynamic measure, unequal-defect diagram, or conjecture about other geometries is certified.
